title: How to apply for your first UK credit card
summary: Check eligibility, understand credit-builder cards and learn what to do about refusals, repayments and disputed payments.
content:
# How to apply for your first UK credit card

Last updated: 2026-11-27

## Before applying
Ask the lender for its minimum age, UK residency, income and address-history requirements. Have your legal name, recent addresses, employment or student status, truthful income and any requested ID ready. If you have just moved, ask whether overseas addresses or alternative ID and address documents are accepted. Register to vote only if eligible. If you cannot register, ask what evidence the lender can use instead. Opening a bank account and being approved for borrowing are separate decisions. [Lender checks](#guide-evidence-eligibility) · [Your credit file](/en/money/uk-credit-history-and-credit-score) · [Opening a bank account](/en/money/open-uk-bank-account-new-arrival)

## Check first, then choose whether to apply
Confirm that the eligibility checker uses a soft search. Its result estimates your chances. A full application normally leaves a hard search. Lenders assess your own circumstances and ability to repay, so no score guarantees acceptance. After a decline, pause rather than sending several more applications. Ask the lender about the reason or agency used and check your reports for wrong addresses, unfamiliar accounts or other mistakes. [Searches and refusals](#guide-evidence-search)

## Credit-builder cards and repayments
A builder card may start with a low limit and charge a high APR. Regular, on-time payments can help build a record when reported. You do not need to pay interest. Utilisation is the amount used relative to your limit; no single percentage applies to every lender. Review the statement balance, minimum and due date. A full-statement Direct Debit can help avoid interest on ordinary purchases if your terms and previous balance allow it. Keep enough in your account and make your first payment manually if the Direct Debit is not yet active. Paying only the minimum can leave debt outstanding for years. [Repayment checks](#guide-evidence-repay)

## Section 75, chargeback and fraud
For breach of contract or misrepresentation, Section 75 may make the lender jointly liable where the cash price of the item or service is more than £100 and no more than £30,000 and the required buyer–lender–supplier link exists. The test is the cash price of the item, rather than the total of unrelated items or the amount charged to the card. A £50 card deposit on a £600 item can qualify if the other conditions are met. Above £30,000, ask about Section 75A if you used a linked credit agreement. A payment intermediary or a purchase for someone else can complicate that link. Chargeback is a card-scheme process with no guaranteed refund and can apply to debit cards too. For purchase disputes, the usual window is around 120 days, but the scheme rules and when it starts can differ. Ask the issuer promptly. Save the receipt and correspondence and contact the card issuer promptly. For an unrecognised payment, freeze the card if possible and contact the issuer using a trusted number. Complain to the firm first, then check Financial Ombudsman Service eligibility and deadlines. [Purchase disputes](#guide-evidence-dispute) · [Unrecognised payments](#guide-evidence-fraud)

## If payments are becoming difficult
This Guide gives general information, without personalised financial advice. Check your own agreement and budget before borrowing. Speak to the lender early if you may miss a payment. Free independent debt advice can help you review your options. [Debt support](#guide-evidence-help)
